covered.hi: Aaj dekha ki sirf barabar tukdon ka fraction naam hota hai, aur neeche wala number saare tukde ginta hai.
covered.en: Today we saw that only equal pieces get a fraction name, and that the bottom number counts all the pieces.

hook.convey: one whole (a roti, a drawn circle) cut and shared → fair only if the pieces are the same size; equal pieces of one whole get the names half, third, quarter; the number of pieces alone does not decide the name

use.hi: Kitchen mein Maa ne garam roti banayi, aur tum do bhai-behen ho: dono ke tukde barabar hone chahiye.
use.en: Mum made a hot roti in the kitchen, and there are two of you: both pieces should be equal.

use.hi: Drawing book mein ek gol roti banao; use barabar tukdon mein baant kar ek tukde mein rang bharenge.
use.en: Draw a round roti in your drawing book; we'll split it into equal pieces and colour one piece.

explain.convey: roti cut into 2 same-size pieces → each piece = half = 1/2; bottom 2 = equal pieces in the whole, top 1 = pieces taken

viewCaption.hi: Wahi roti ab ek patti ban gayi hai: do barabar tukde, ek mein rang, ek bina rang ka. Dono tukde ek jitne lambe hain.
viewCaption.en: The same roti is now a strip: two equal pieces, one coloured, one uncoloured. Both pieces are the same length.

point.hi: Yeh roti 2 barabar tukdon mein kati hai, aur ek tukde mein rang hai. Fraction mein neeche wala number roti ke kul barabar tukde ginta hai, upar wala number, jitne tukde humne liye.
point.en: This roti is cut into 2 equal pieces, and one piece is coloured. In a fraction the bottom number counts all the roti's equal pieces, the top number the pieces we took.

pointAlt.hi: Ek laddoo se socho: tumne jitne tukde uthaye, woh ginti upar likhte hain. Neeche woh ginti jaati hai ki poora laddoo kitne barabar tukdon mein toda gaya.
pointAlt.en: Think of a laddoo: how many pieces you picked up is written on top. Below goes how many equal pieces the whole laddoo was broken into.

prompt.hi: Ek tukda rangin hai, ek bina rang ka. Toh rangin tukda roti ka kaunsa fraction hai?
prompt.en: One piece is coloured, one is not. So what fraction of the roti is the coloured piece?

why.hi: rangin tukda roti ke 2 barabar tukdon mein se 1 hai, toh 1/2, yaani aadha; neeche wala number 2 hai
why.en: the coloured piece is 1 of the roti's 2 equal pieces, so 1/2, a half; the bottom number is 2

whyShort.hi: roti ke 2 barabar tukdon mein se 1, yaani 1/2
whyShort.en: 1 of the roti's 2 equal pieces, so 1/2

whyAlt.hi: 1/1 ka matlab hota poori roti, par rangin tukda toh roti ka sirf ek aadha hai
whyAlt.en: 1/1 would mean the whole roti, but the coloured piece is only one half of it

simpler.hi: Roti ke saare tukde ungli se gino, phir sirf rang wale. Dono gintiyan fraction mein kahan jaati hain, yeh socho.
simpler.en: Count all the roti's pieces with your finger, then only the coloured ones. Think where the two counts go in the fraction.

simpler.hi: Roti ke dono tukde ek jitne hain, isliye dono ka naam ek hi hai. Woh naam is baat se banta hai ki roti kitne tukdon mein kati.
simpler.en: The roti's two pieces are the same size, so both have the same name. That name comes from how many pieces the roti is cut into.

explain.convey: a pizza and a cake, 3 pieces each, but only same-size pieces get the name third: the cake's equal pieces are each 1/3; the pizza has one big and two small pieces → asked: is a small one a third

viewCaption.hi: Pizza aur cake ab do patti ban gaye hain, pizza pehli patti mein aur cake doosri mein. Dono pattiyon ke teen-teen tukde hain.
viewCaption.en: The pizza and the cake are now two strips, the pizza first and the cake second. Each strip has three pieces.

point.hi: Yeh pizza aur yeh cake, dono ke 3-3 tukde. Cake ke teeno tukde barabar hain, toh wahan har tukda ek-tihaai hai, 1/3. Pizza mein ek tukda bada hai aur do chhote.
point.en: Here's a pizza and a cake, 3 pieces each. The cake's three pieces are equal, so there each piece is one-third, 1/3. The pizza has one big piece and two small ones.

pointAlt.hi: Ek-tihaai ki jaanch aise hoti hai: ek tukda utha kar baaki do tukdon se milao. Cake ka har tukda baaki dono se bilkul milta hai, isliye cake ka har tukda 1/3 hai. Yahi jaanch pizza ke tukdon par karke dekho.
pointAlt.en: This is how you test for a third: pick up one piece and hold it against the other two. Each cake piece matches the other two exactly, so each cake piece is 1/3. Try the same test on the pizza's pieces.

prompt.hi: Pizza ka ek chhota tukda lo. Kya woh pizza ka ek-tihaai hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Take a small piece of the pizza. Is it one-third of the pizza, yes or no?

reask.hi: Kya pizza ka ek chhota tukda poore pizza ka ek-tihaai hai?
reask.en: Is a small piece of the pizza one-third of the whole pizza?

accept: no, the pieces are not equal

why.hi: pizza ke tukde chhote-bade hain, aur ek-tihaai tabhi banta hai jab 3 tukde barabar hon
why.en: the pizza's pieces are big and small, and a third needs 3 equal pieces

whyShort.hi: ek-tihaai ke liye 3 barabar tukde chahiye; yeh chhote-bade hain
whyShort.en: a third needs 3 equal pieces; these are not

whyAlt.hi: chhota tukda ek-tihaai hota toh teen chhote tukde milkar poora pizza bana dete, par yahan ek tukda bada hai
whyAlt.en: if a small piece were a third, three small pieces would make the whole pizza, but here one piece is big

simpler.hi: Pizza ka chhota tukda uske bade tukde ke saath milaa kar dekho. Phir cake ke tukdon ko aapas mein milao.
simpler.en: Hold the pizza's small piece against its big piece. Then compare the cake's pieces with each other.

viewCaption.hi: Pehli patti pizza hai: uska ek tukda lamba hai aur do chhote. Doosri patti, cake, ke teeno tukde ek jitne lambe hain.
viewCaption.en: The first strip is the pizza: one of its pieces is long and two are short. The second strip, the cake, has three pieces of the same length.

simpler.hi: Ek-tihaai ka naam do baaton se milta hai: poori cheez ke 3 tukde, aur teeno ek jitne bade. Cake mein yeh dono baatein hain.
simpler.en: The name one-third needs two things: the whole in 3 pieces, and all three the same size. The cake has both.

explain.convey: drawn circle in 3 equal parts → one part = one-third = 1/3; bottom 3 = all the equal parts of the whole

viewCaption.hi: Wahi circle ab patti mein khula hai: teen barabar tukde, ek mein rang, do bina rang ke.
viewCaption.en: The same circle is laid out as a strip: three equal pieces, one coloured, two uncoloured.

point.hi: Is circle ke 3 barabar tukde hain, ek mein rang. Yeh rangin tukda ek-tihaai hai, 1/3. Neeche wala number 3 isliye hai, kyunki poore circle ke 3 barabar tukde hain.
point.en: This circle has 3 equal pieces, one coloured. That coloured piece is one-third, 1/3. The bottom number is 3 because the whole circle has 3 equal pieces.

pointAlt.hi: Seedhi baat: circle ke 3 barabar tukde hain, aur 1 mein rang. Isliye 1/3: neeche 3, upar 1.
pointAlt.en: Plainly: the circle has 3 equal pieces, and 1 is coloured. So 1/3: 3 at the bottom, 1 on top.

prompt.hi: Ek aur tukde mein rang bharo. Ab rangin tukde poore circle ka kaunsa fraction hain?
prompt.en: Colour one more piece. Now what fraction of the whole circle are the coloured pieces?

reask.hi: Ek aur tukde mein rang bharne ke baad, rangin tukde poore circle ka kaunsa fraction hain?
reask.en: After colouring one more piece, what fraction of the whole circle are the coloured pieces?

why.hi: circle 3 barabar tukdon mein bata hai aur ab 2 mein rang hai, yaani 2/3
why.en: the circle has 3 equal pieces and 2 are coloured now, so 2/3

whyShort.hi: 3 barabar tukdon mein se 2 mein rang, yaani 2/3
whyShort.en: 2 of the 3 equal pieces are coloured, so 2/3

whyAlt.hi: sirf ek tukda bina rang ka bacha, toh rangin tukde poore circle se ek-tihaai kam hain: 2/3
whyAlt.en: only one piece is left uncoloured, so the coloured pieces are one-third less than the whole circle: 2/3

simpler.hi: Pehle gino ki circle ke kul kitne tukde hain. Phir socho, ek aur tukda rangne ke baad kitne tukde rangin honge.
simpler.en: First count how many pieces the circle has in all. Then think how many pieces will be coloured once one more is coloured.

simpler.hi: Ek kaagaz ko teen barabar tukdon mein modo, aur ek tukde par rang karo. Woh rangin tukda kaagaz ka 1/3 hai.
simpler.en: Fold a sheet of paper into three equal pieces, and colour one piece. That coloured piece is 1/3 of the paper.

explain.convey: strip in 8 equal parts, 1 shaded → one-eighth = 1/8; bottom = all 8 parts of the whole, never the 7 unshaded parts left → not 1/7; then an error spot on a second strip (a ribbon of 6 equal pieces, 1 cut off for Raju, 5 left): Raju's 1/5 is judged → no, 1/6

viewCaption.hi: Yeh patti yahan ek number line ban gayi hai, 0 se 1 tak, aath barabar gap. Pehle gap ke ant mein 1/8 ka mark hai.
viewCaption.en: The strip has become a number line here, from 0 to 1, eight equal gaps. At the end of the first gap is the 1/8 mark.

point.hi: Is patti ka rangin tukda 1/8 hai: 8 saare tukde ginta hai, bache hue 7 nahi.
point.en: This strip's coloured piece is 1/8: the 8 counts all the pieces, not the 7 left over.

pointAlt.hi: Ek kitaab ke 8 barabar panne socho, aur ek panna phat gaya. Woh panna kitaab ka 1/8 tha, kyunki kitaab 8 pannon se bani thi; bache hue 7 panne uska naam nahi badalte.
pointAlt.en: Picture a book of 8 equal pages, and one page tore out. That page was 1/8 of the book, because the book was made of 8 pages; the 7 pages left do not change its name.

prompt.hi: Doosri patti ke 6 barabar tukde hain. Raju ne 1 tukda kaat kar le liya, 5 bache. Raju kehta hai usne patti ka 1/5 liya, kyunki 5 tukde bache. Kya Raju sahi hai?
prompt.en: The second strip has 6 equal pieces. Raju cut off 1 piece and took it, 5 were left. Raju says he took 1/5 of the strip, because 5 pieces were left. Is Raju right?

reask.hi: 6 barabar tukdon wali patti se 1 tukda kata aur 5 bache, toh kya Raju ne patti ka 1/5 liya?
reask.en: If 1 piece was cut from a strip of 6 equal pieces and 5 were left, did Raju take 1/5 of the strip?

why.hi: Raju ka tukda patti ke 6 tukdon mein se 1 hai, toh 1/6, 1/5 nahi; bache hue 5 tukde naam nahi badalte
why.en: Raju's piece is 1 of the strip's 6 pieces, so 1/6, not 1/5; the 5 pieces left do not change the name

whyShort.hi: Raju ka tukda 6 tukdon mein se 1, yaani 1/6
whyShort.en: Raju's piece is 1 of 6 pieces, so 1/6

whyAlt.hi: kaatne se pehle patti ke 6 tukde the, aur Raju ka tukda unmein se ek hai; kitne bache, isse naam nahi badalta
whyAlt.en: before the cut the strip had 6 pieces, and Raju's piece is one of them; how many are left does not change the name

simpler.hi: Kaatne se pehle doosri patti mein kitne tukde the, woh gino. Phir use Raju ke 5 se milao.
simpler.en: Count how many pieces the second strip had before the cut. Then compare that with Raju's 5.

viewCaption.hi: Raju wali patti yahan number line ke neeche hai: 0 se 1 tak, chhe barabar gap. Line ke upar wahi aath gap hain, aur un par 1/8 ka mark.
viewCaption.en: Raju's strip is below the number line here: 0 to 1, six equal gaps. Above the line are the same eight gaps, with the 1/8 mark on them.

simpler.hi: Bina rang ke tukde gino, 7, phir rangin tukda bhi jodo, 8: 1/8 ka 8 yahi poori ginti hai.
simpler.en: Count the uncoloured pieces, 7, then add the coloured piece too, 8: the 8 of 1/8 is this full count.

problem.hi: Ek lambi barfi ke 5 barabar tukde kiye, aur 3 tukde kha liye.
problem.en: A long barfi was cut into 5 equal pieces, and 3 pieces were eaten.

problemAlt.hi: Board par barfi dekho: rangin tukde plate par bache hain, aur bina rang ke tukde kha liye gaye. Hum do gintiyan karenge, saare tukde aur bache hue tukde, aur unhi se fraction banega.
problemAlt.en: Look at the barfi on the board: the coloured pieces are left on the plate, and the uncoloured ones were eaten. We will make two counts, all the pieces and the pieces left, and the fraction comes from those.

simpler.hi: Pehle ek chhoti baat yaad karo: roti ke 2 barabar tukdon mein se 1 bacha, toh roti ka 1/2 bacha. Barfi mein bhi wahi karna hai: saare tukde neeche wale number mein, bache hue upar wale number mein.
simpler.en: First recall a small one: if 1 of a roti's 2 equal pieces is left, 1/2 of the roti is left. The barfi works the same: all the pieces in the bottom number, the ones left in the top number.

givens.hi: Hamare paas do cheezein hain: poori barfi ke tukde, aur khaye hue tukde.
givens.en: We know two things: the pieces of the whole barfi, and the pieces eaten.

find.en: the pieces left, as a fraction

prompt.hi: Neeche wale number mein kaunse tukde ginoge: saare, ya sirf khaye hue?
prompt.en: Which pieces does the bottom number count: all, or only the eaten?

right.hi: Haan, saare tukde: barfi 5 barabar tukdon mein kati thi.
right.en: Yes, all the pieces: the barfi was cut into 5 equal pieces.

do.hi: Neeche wala number poori barfi ke tukde ginta hai
do.en: The bottom number counts the whole barfi's pieces

why.hi: barfi khaane se pehle 5 barabar tukdon mein kati thi
why.en: before anyone ate, the barfi was cut into 5 equal pieces

simpler.hi: Khaane se pehle wali poori barfi socho: uske saare tukde gino.
simpler.en: Think of the whole barfi before anyone ate: count all its pieces.

prompt.hi: Tumhari baari: plate par bache tukde poori barfi ka kaunsa fraction hain?
prompt.en: Your turn: what fraction of the whole barfi are the pieces left on the plate?

reask.hi: Plate par bache tukde poori barfi ka kaunsa fraction hain?
reask.en: What fraction of the whole barfi are the pieces left on the plate?

why.hi: barfi ke 5 barabar tukde the aur unmein se 2 bache, isliye neeche wala number 5 aur upar wala 2
why.en: the barfi had 5 equal pieces and 2 are left, so the bottom number is 5 and the top 2

whyAlt.hi: khaye hue 3 tukde neeche nahi jaate; neeche hamesha poori barfi ke saare tukde aate hain, 5, toh 2/5
whyAlt.en: the 3 eaten pieces do not go at the bottom; the bottom always takes all the whole barfi's pieces, 5, so 2/5

simpler.hi: Pehle gino plate par kitne tukde bache; woh ginti upar jaati hai, aur neeche saare 5.
simpler.en: First count how many pieces are left on the plate; that count goes on top, and all 5 at the bottom.

viewCaption.hi: Is circle ke saare tukde barabar hain. Rangin tukde plate par bache hue hain, aur bina rang ke tukde kha liye gaye.
viewCaption.en: All the pieces of this circle are equal. The coloured pieces are the ones left on the plate, and the uncoloured ones were eaten.

answer.hi: bache hue tukde barfi ka 2/5 hain
answer.en: the pieces left are 2/5 of the barfi

why.hi: 5 barabar tukdon mein se 2 bache; khaye hue 3 tukde neeche wale number mein nahi jaate
why.en: 2 of the 5 equal pieces are left; the 3 eaten pieces do not go in the bottom number

viewCaption.hi: Wahi barfi ab ek circle ki tarah bani hai: paanch barabar tukde, unmein se do mein rang. Rangin tukde plate par bache hue hain.
viewCaption.en: The same barfi is now drawn like a circle: five equal pieces, two of them coloured. The coloured pieces are the ones left on the plate.

prompt.hi: Laddoo toota aur 3 tukde ho gaye, ek bada aur do chhote. Board par dekho: bada tukda laddoo ka 1/2 hai ya 1/3?
prompt.en: A laddoo broke into 3 pieces, one big and two small. Look at the board: is the big piece 1/2 or 1/3 of the laddoo?

did.hi: toote laddoo ka bada tukda poore laddoo se milaya
did.en: compared the big piece of a broken laddoo with the whole laddoo

viewCaption.hi: Laddoo ab ek patti mein hai, teen tukdon mein: ek lamba aur do chhote, aur teeno milkar poora laddoo.
viewCaption.en: The laddoo is now one strip, in three pieces: one long and two short, and all three together make the whole laddoo.

why.hi: laddoo ke 3 tukdon mein bada tukda theek aadha hai, yaani 1/2; dono chhote milkar baaki aadha
why.en: of the laddoo's 3 pieces, the big one is exactly half, 1/2; the two small ones make the other half

whyShort.hi: bada tukda theek aadha laddoo hai, yaani 1/2
whyShort.en: the big piece is exactly half the laddoo, 1/2

whyAlt.hi: teen tukde hain par barabar nahi, isliye 1/3 nahi; bada tukda laddoo ka theek aadha gherta hai, 1/2
whyAlt.en: there are three pieces but not equal ones, so not 1/3; the big piece covers exactly half the laddoo, 1/2

answerViewCaption.hi: Patti mein laddoo ka lamba tukda dekho: woh akela utna hai jitne dono chhote tukde milkar, isliye woh 1/2 hai.
answerViewCaption.en: Look at the laddoo's long piece in the strip: on its own it is as much as the two small pieces together, so it is 1/2.

simpler.hi: Dono chhote tukde jodo aur bade tukde se milao. Phir dekho, bada tukda poore laddoo ka kitna gherta hai.
simpler.en: Put the two small pieces together and match them with the big one. Then see how much of the whole laddoo the big piece covers.

prompt.hi: Tumhari chocolate ke 12 barabar tukde hain. Tumne usmein se 1/12 kha liya. Ab kitne tukde bache?
prompt.en: Your chocolate has 12 equal pieces. You ate 1/12 of it. How many pieces are left now?

reask.hi: 12 barabar tukdon wali chocolate ka 1/12 khaya gaya, toh kitne tukde bache?
reask.en: 1/12 of a chocolate of 12 equal pieces was eaten: how many pieces are left?

did.hi: 1/12 khaane ke baad chocolate ke bache hue tukde gine
did.en: counted the chocolate pieces left after eating 1/12

viewCaption.hi: Wahi chocolate ab ek circle mein hai, 12 barabar tukdon mein. Abhi kisi tukde mein rang nahi bhara.
viewCaption.en: The same chocolate is now a circle, in 12 equal pieces. No piece is coloured yet.

why.hi: 1/12 ka matlab chocolate ke 12 barabar tukdon mein se 1 khaya; 12 mein se 1 gaya, toh 11 bache
why.en: 1/12 means 1 of the chocolate's 12 equal pieces was eaten; 1 of 12 went, so 11 are left

whyShort.hi: 12 tukdon mein se 1 khaya, toh 11 bache
whyShort.en: 1 of 12 pieces was eaten, so 11 are left

whyAlt.hi: 1/12 ka neeche wala number, 12, saare tukde ginta hai, bache hue nahi; upar wala number 1 batata hai ki unmein se ek khaya, toh baaki 11 bache
whyAlt.en: the bottom number of 1/12, 12, counts all the pieces, not the ones left; the top number 1 says one of them was eaten, so the other 11 are left

answerViewCaption.hi: Circle ke 12 barabar tukdon mein se ek mein rang hai, woh khaya hua 1/12 hai. Baaki 11 tukde bache hain.
answerViewCaption.en: One of the circle's 12 equal pieces is coloured, that is the 1/12 eaten. The other 11 pieces are left.

simpler.hi: Socho, 1/12 ka neeche wala number kya ginta hai, aur upar wala kya ginta hai.
simpler.en: Think what the bottom number of 1/12 counts, and what the top one counts.

prompt.hi: Cake ke 4 tukde hue: ek bada aur teen chhote. Ek chhota tukda cake ke 1/4 se kam hai, 1/4 ke barabar hai, ya 1/4 se zyada?
prompt.en: A cake was cut into 4 pieces: one big and three small. Is one small piece less than 1/4 of the cake, equal to it, or more than 1/4?

reask.hi: Ek bade aur teen chhote tukdon wale cake mein, ek chhota tukda 1/4 se kam hai, barabar hai, ya zyada?
reask.en: In a cake of one big and three small pieces, is one small piece less than 1/4, equal to it, or more?

did.hi: chhote-bade tukdon wale cake ka chhota tukda 1/4 se milaya
did.en: compared a small piece of an uneven cake with 1/4

viewCaption.hi: Cake ab ek patti ki shakal mein hai: ek lamba tukda aur teen chhote tukde, sab ek hi patti mein.
viewCaption.en: The cake is now shaped as one strip: one long piece and three short pieces, all in the one strip.

why.hi: chaaron tukde milkar poora cake hain aur bada tukda baaki se bada hai, toh har chhota tukda 1/4 se kam
why.en: four pieces make the whole cake and one is bigger than the rest, so each small one is under 1/4

whyShort.hi: ek tukda bada hai, isliye har chhota 1/4 se kam
whyShort.en: one is bigger, so a small one is under 1/4

whyAlt.hi: charon tukde barabar hote toh har ek 1/4 hota; yahan bada tukda zyada le gaya, toh chhote tukde 1/4 se chhote reh gaye
whyAlt.en: if all four pieces were equal each would be 1/4; here the big piece took more, so the small ones are left smaller than 1/4

answerViewCaption.hi: Doosri patti mein chaar barabar tukde hain, aur rangin tukda 1/4 hai. Pehli patti ka chhota tukda us rangin tukde se chhota hai, isliye 1/4 se kam.
answerViewCaption.en: The second strip has four equal pieces, and the coloured piece is 1/4. A small piece of the first strip is shorter than that coloured piece, so less than 1/4.

simpler.hi: Socho, chaaron tukde barabar hote toh har ek kitna hota. Phir dekho, bade tukde ne baaki teen ke liye kitni jagah chhodi.
simpler.en: Think how big each piece would be if all four were equal. Then see how much room the big piece left for the other three.

ladder.why: more than one part taken → 3 of 4 equal parts = 3/4; top number beyond 1
error spot: parts left used as bottom → bottom = whole's equal parts
harder contrast with quarters on flags → equality decides, count alone does not

remediation.move: fair-sharing story, imagined: a rope cut into 1 long piece + some short ones → not a fair split → counting the pieces does not name them as fractions; then a sheet of paper folded down the middle and cut into 2 same-size pieces → only then is each piece a half → first check the pieces are the same size; then the torn roti on the board, asked as a direct claim (is the bigger piece more than half?)

say.hi: Yeh rassi ek lambe aur do chhote tukdon mein kati, isliye in tukdon ka fraction naam nahi hota. Kaagaz beech se kata, dono tukde ek jaise, toh unka fraction naam hai.
say.en: This rope is cut into one long piece and two short ones, so these pieces get no fraction name. The paper is cut down the middle, both pieces alike, so they have a fraction name.

viewCaption.hi: Rassi aur kaagaz yahan do patti ban gaye hain: rassi ka ek tukda lamba aur do chhote, kaagaz ke dono tukde ek jitne.
viewCaption.en: The rope and the paper are two strips here: the rope has one long piece and two short ones, the paper's two pieces are the same.

sayAlt.hi: Ek seb ko 3 tukdon mein kaato, ek mota aur do patle. Tukde 3 hain, par inhe ek-tihaai nahi kehte, kyunki ek-tihaai tabhi hota hai jab teeno ek jitne hon.
sayAlt.en: Cut an apple into 3 pieces, one thick and two thin. There are 3 pieces, but they are not called thirds, because a third needs all three to be the same size.

viewCaption.hi: Seb yahan ek patti ban gaya hai: ek mota tukda aur do patle tukde.
viewCaption.en: The apple is a strip here: one thick piece and two thin pieces.

simpler.hi: Chhote-bade tukde gin kar naam nahi rakhte; pehle dekho, tukde ek size ke hain ya nahi, jaise kaagaz ke do aadhe.
simpler.en: You can't name big-and-small pieces by counting them; first check whether the pieces are the same size, like the paper's two halves.

prompt.hi: Roti ke 2 tukde hue: ek bada, ek chhota. Kya bada tukda roti ke aadhe se zyada hai?
prompt.en: A roti tears into 2 pieces, one bigger, one smaller. Is the bigger piece more than half the roti?

accept: yes, it is more than half

viewCaption.hi: Patti mein roti ke do tukde dekho: lamba tukda ek taraf, chhota doosri taraf, aur dono milkar poori roti.
viewCaption.en: Look at the roti's two pieces in the strip: the long one on one side, the short one on the other, and together the whole roti.

why.hi: do tukde barabar hon tabhi har ek aadha hota; yahan bada tukda chhote se bada hai, toh aadhe se zyada
why.en: two pieces are halves only when equal; here the bigger one is more than the smaller, so it is more than half

whyShort.hi: tukde barabar nahi; bada tukda aadhe se zyada hai
whyShort.en: unequal pieces; the big one is over half

whyAlt.hi: aadha tab hota jab dono tukde ek jitne hote; bada tukda chhote se zyada roti le gaya, isliye woh aadhe se aage nikal gaya
whyAlt.en: it would be a half only if both pieces were the same; the bigger piece took more roti than the smaller, so it goes past the half

answerViewCaption.hi: Doosri patti do barabar aadhon mein hai. Pehli patti ka lamba tukda us aadhe se aage tak jaata hai, isliye woh aadhe se zyada hai.
answerViewCaption.en: The second strip is in two equal halves. The first strip's long piece goes past that half, so it is more than half.

simpler.hi: Roti ke beech mein ek line socho jo use do barabar aadhon mein baante. Ab dekho, bada tukda us line par rukta hai ya usse aage jaata hai.
simpler.en: Imagine a line through the middle of the roti that splits it into two equal halves. Now see whether the big piece stops at that line or goes past it.

remediation.move: name the piece first: in a whole of equal pieces the bottom number says how many equal pieces the whole was cut into, eaten or left → the top only counts the pieces asked about; then the then-card's chocolate of 4 pieces with 2 coloured (eaten): Pinky's 2/4 or Golu's 2/2

say.hi: Socho, chocolate ke saare tukde barabar hain. Neeche wala number poori chocolate ke tukde ginta hai; kuch tukde kha lo, woh ginti wahi rehti hai.
say.en: Picture a chocolate whose pieces are all equal. The bottom number counts the whole chocolate's pieces; eat some pieces and that count still stays the same.

sayAlt.hi: Ek roti 8 barabar tukdon mein kati socho. Usmein se 3 kha lo ya 5, roti phir bhi 8 tukdon se hi bani thi, isliye neeche wala number 8 hi rehta hai, aur upar wala number sirf khaye hue tukde ginta hai.
sayAlt.en: Picture a roti cut into 8 equal pieces. Eat 3 of them or 5, the roti was still made of 8 pieces, so the bottom number stays 8, and the top number counts only the eaten pieces.

viewCaption.hi: Roti yahan ek patti ban gayi hai: aath barabar tukde, aur rangin tukde khaye hue.
viewCaption.en: The roti is a strip here: eight equal pieces, and the coloured pieces are eaten.

simpler.hi: Khaane se pehle wali poori chocolate ke saare tukde neeche wale number mein jaate hain. Upar wale number mein sirf woh tukde, jinki baat poochhi gayi hai.
simpler.en: All the pieces of the whole chocolate, before anyone ate, go in the bottom number. The top number holds only the pieces the question is about.

prompt.hi: Is chocolate ke rangin tukde khaye gaye. Pinky kehti hai 2/4, Golu kehta hai 2/2. Kiska sahi hai, Pinky ka ya Golu ka?
prompt.en: The coloured pieces of this chocolate were eaten. Pinky says 2/4, Golu says 2/2. Who is right, Pinky or Golu?

reask.hi: Is chocolate ke rangin tukde khaye gaye: Pinky ka 2/4 sahi hai ya Golu ka 2/2?
reask.en: This chocolate's coloured pieces were eaten: is Pinky's 2/4 right or Golu's 2/2?

viewCaption.hi: Yahan chocolate ek circle ki tarah bani hai: chaar barabar tukde, do mein rang, do bina rang ke. Rangin tukde woh hain jo khaye gaye.
viewCaption.en: Here the chocolate is drawn like a circle: four equal pieces, two coloured, two uncoloured. The coloured pieces are the ones that were eaten.

why.hi: khaye hue 2 tukde chocolate ke 4 barabar tukdon mein se hain, toh 2/4; bache hue 2 neeche wala number nahi
why.en: the 2 eaten pieces are 2 of the chocolate's 4 equal pieces, so 2/4; the 2 left are not the bottom number

whyShort.hi: 4 barabar tukdon mein se 2 khaye, yaani 2/4
whyShort.en: 2 of the 4 equal pieces were eaten, so 2/4

whyAlt.hi: 2/2 ka matlab poori chocolate hoti, par poori chocolate toh khayi nahi gayi; isliye Golu galat hai aur Pinky sahi
whyAlt.en: 2/2 would mean the whole chocolate, but the whole chocolate was not eaten; so Golu is wrong and Pinky is right

answerViewCaption.hi: Number line par 0 se 1 tak chaar barabar gap hain, aur 2/4 ka mark do gap par hai. Khaye hue 2 tukde 4 mein se 2 hain, isliye 2/4.
answerViewCaption.en: On the number line there are four equal gaps from 0 to 1, and the 2/4 mark is two gaps along. The 2 eaten pieces are 2 of 4, so 2/4.

simpler.hi: Board par chocolate ke saare tukde gino, rangin bhi aur bina rang ke bhi. Phir sirf rangin tukde gino.
simpler.en: Count all the chocolate's pieces on the board, coloured and uncoloured. Then count just the coloured ones.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab ek cheez ki jagah bahut saari cheezein lenge, jaise laddoo, aam ya kanche, aur unka fraction nikalenge. Niyam wahi rahega: sab barabar.
bridgeToNext.en: Next, in place of one thing we take lots of things, like laddoos, mangoes or marbles, and find fractions of them. The rule stays the same: everything equal.

simpler.hi: Ab bahut saari cheezon ka fraction dekhenge.
simpler.en: Now we look at fractions of lots of things.

covered.hi: Phir group ka fraction aaya: neeche wala number barabar group ginta hai, aur ek group ki ginti jawab hai.
covered.en: Then the fraction of a group: the bottom number counts the equal groups, and one group's count is the answer.

hook.convey: 12 laddoos (or 12 biscuits), 2 sharers, fair share → each share = half of the set; a fraction can be of a whole set, the set being the one whole

use.hi: Kitchen ke dibbe mein 12 laddoo hain, aur khaane wale tum do; kisi ko kam nahi milna chahiye.
use.en: There are 12 laddoos in the kitchen tin, and two of you to eat them; nobody should get less.

use.hi: Cricket match ke baad 2 bhookhe bachche ghar aaye; dibbe ke 12 laddoo dono ko ek jitne milne chahiye.
use.en: After a cricket match 2 hungry children come home; the tin's 12 laddoos must go to both equally.

explain.convey: the tin's 12 laddoos, loose on the board → half = 2 equal groups, one group's count is the half; check: both shares together make all 12 again; the ask finds the half

viewCaption.hi: Board par 12 laddoo 3 qatar mein rakhe hain, har qatar mein 4. Har laddoo ka apna khana hai.
viewCaption.en: The board has 12 laddoos in three rows, four in each row. Each laddoo has its own box.

point.hi: Do bachche yeh 12 laddoo barabar baantenge. Aadha matlab: dono ke paas ek jitne laddoo, aur ek bachche ke laddoo hi aadha. Jaanch: dono ke laddoo jodo, toh saare 12 wapas.
point.en: Two children will share these 12 laddoos equally. Half means: both have the same number, and one child's laddoos are the half. The check: put both children's laddoos together and all 12 are back.

pointAlt.hi: Aadha karne ka ek aur tareeka: laddoo ek-ek karke do group mein baari-baari rakho, jab tak sab khatam na ho jaayein. Dono group mein ek jitne laddoo aayenge, aur ek group ke laddoo hi aadha hain.
pointAlt.en: Another way to halve: put the laddoos one at a time into two groups, taking turns, until they are all gone. Both groups get the same number, and one group's laddoos are the half.

prompt.hi: 12 laddoo ka aadha kitne laddoo hai?
prompt.en: How many laddoos is half of 12 laddoos?

why.hi: 12 laddoo 2 barabar group mein jaayein toh har group mein 6, aur 2 × 6 = 12
why.en: 12 laddoos in 2 equal groups puts 6 in each, and 2 × 6 = 12

whyShort.hi: 2 barabar group, har ek mein 6 laddoo
whyShort.en: 2 equal groups, 6 laddoos in each

whyAlt.hi: laddoo ek-ek karke do group mein rakho toh har group mein 6 aate hain; 6 aur 6 milkar 12
whyAlt.en: put the laddoos one at a time into two groups and each group gets 6; 6 and 6 make 12

simpler.hi: Board par laddoo teen line mein hain, har line mein 4. Har line ko beech se do-do mein baanto, aur ek taraf ke laddoo gino.
simpler.en: On the board the laddoos are in three rows of 4. Split each row in the middle, two and two, and count the laddoos on one side.

viewCaption.hi: Yeh wahi 12 laddoo hain: 3 qatarein, har qatar mein 4. Inhe ek-ek karke do group mein rakhna hai.
viewCaption.en: These are the same 12 laddoos, three rows of four. They are to go into two groups one at a time.

simpler.hi: Ek chhoti ginti se socho: chaar laddoo do bachchon mein barabar bate, toh dono ko do-do mile. Do aur do jodo toh chaar wapas, aur ek bachche ke do laddoo hi chaar ka aadha hain.
simpler.en: Think with a small count: four laddoos shared equally by two children gives each two. Put two and two together and the four are back, and one child's two laddoos are half of four.

explain.convey: 24 mangoes shown as 1/6 (6 equal groups of 4): bottom 6 = share into 6 equal groups, top 1 = take one group; then 1/3 of the same 24: bottom 3 = 3 equal groups, one group's count is the answer

viewCaption.hi: Chhe group ab ek jaal mein hain: har qatar ek group hai, aur har qatar mein chaar aam.
viewCaption.en: The six groups are now in one grid: each row is a group, with four mangoes in each row.

point.hi: Yeh 24 aam 6 barabar group mein hain. 1/6 ka matlab: 6 barabar group banao aur ek group lo, toh 24 ka 1/6 hai 4 aam. Chhote group jod kar bade barabar group bhi bante hain: teen-teen group milao, toh har bada group 24 ka 1/2 hai.
point.en: These 24 mangoes are in 6 equal groups. 1/6 means: make 6 equal groups and take one group, so 1/6 of 24 is 4 mangoes. Small groups can be joined into bigger equal groups too: put the groups together three at a time, and each big group is 1/2 of 24.

pointAlt.hi: Socho, 6 bachche yeh 24 aam barabar baantein: har bachche ko ek group milta hai, 4 aam. Yahi 24 ka 1/6 hai.
pointAlt.en: Picture 6 children sharing these 24 mangoes equally: each child gets one group, 4 mangoes. That is 1/6 of 24.

prompt.hi: 24 ka 1/3 lena hai. Board ke 6 group mein se kitne group uthaoge?
prompt.en: We want 1/3 of 24. How many of the board's 6 groups do you pick up?

reask.hi: 24 aam ke 6 barabar group mein se, 24 ka 1/3 lene ke liye kitne group uthaoge?
reask.en: Of the 6 equal groups of 24 mangoes, how many groups do you pick up to take 1/3 of 24?

why.hi: 6 group ko jod kar 3 barabar bade group banao: har bade group mein 2 group, yaani 8 aam
why.en: join the 6 groups into 3 equal bigger groups: each bigger group holds 2 groups, which is 8 mangoes

whyShort.hi: 6 group se 3 bade group, har ek mein 2
whyShort.en: 6 groups make 3 bigger groups, 2 in each

whyAlt.hi: 3 bachche 6 group baantein toh har bachche ko 2 group milte hain, 4 aur 4 aam, yaani 8
whyAlt.en: if 3 children share the 6 groups, each child gets 2 groups, 4 and 4 mangoes, which is 8

simpler.hi: 6 group ko 3 bachchon mein ek-ek karke baanto. Ek bachche ke paas kitne group aaye, woh gino.
simpler.en: Hand out the 6 groups to 3 children, one at a time. Count how many groups one child gets.

viewCaption.hi: Jaal mein chhe qatarein hain, har qatar ek group, aur kul 24 aam. Ek qatar uthana matlab ek group uthana.
viewCaption.en: The grid has six rows, each row a group, and 24 mangoes in all. Picking up one row means picking up one group.

simpler.hi: Group-group karke 4 aam jodte jao jab tak 24 na ho jaayein: aise 6 group lagte hain. Isliye ek group, 4 aam, 24 ka 1/6 hai.
simpler.en: Keep adding 4 mangoes, group by group, until you reach 24: it takes 6 such groups. So one group, 4 mangoes, is 1/6 of 24.

explain.convey: 20 marbles shown as half (2 equal groups of 10, the bottom 2 of 1/2) → method: bottom number → that many equal groups → one group's size is the answer; and backwards: a group's size → count the groups → the bottom number; asked backwards: 5 of the 20 is which fraction

viewCaption.hi: Do group ab ek jaal mein hain: do qatarein, har qatar mein das kanche.
viewCaption.en: The two groups are now in one grid: two rows, ten marbles in each row.

point.hi: Yeh 20 kanche 2 barabar group mein hain. Ek group ke 10 kanche 20 ka aadha hain, 1/2. Group ka size pata ho, toh aise group gino: wahi ginti neeche wala number hai.
point.en: These 20 marbles are in 2 equal groups. One group's 10 marbles are half of 20, 1/2. If you know a group's size, count such groups: that count is the bottom number.

pointAlt.hi: Ise paison se socho: 20 rupaye ke 10-10 rupaye ke dher banao, toh 2 dher bante hain, isliye 10 rupaye 20 ka 1/2 hain. Dher ka size pata ho, toh dher gino; wahi ginti neeche wala number hai.
pointAlt.en: Think of it with money: make piles of 10 rupees out of 20 rupees and you get 2 piles, so 10 rupees is 1/2 of 20. When you know a pile's size, count the piles; that count is the bottom number.

prompt.hi: Socho, yeh 20 kanche kuch bachchon mein barabar bate, aur har bachche ko 5 mile. 5 kanche saare 20 kanchon ka kaunsa fraction hain?
prompt.en: Imagine these 20 marbles were shared equally among some children, and each child got 5. What fraction of all 20 marbles are 5 marbles?

why.hi: 4 × 5 = 20, toh 20 kanche 4 bachchon mein barabar batte hain; har bachche ke 5 kanche 1/4 hain
why.en: 4 × 5 = 20, so 20 marbles go equally to 4 children; each child's 5 marbles are 1/4

whyShort.hi: 4 × 5 = 20, toh 4 bachche, har ek ka 1/4
whyShort.en: 4 × 5 = 20, so 4 children, each gets 1/4

whyAlt.hi: 20 ka aadha 10, aur 10 ka aadha 5; toh 5 kanche aadhe ka bhi aadha hain, yaani 1/4
whyAlt.en: half of 20 is 10, and half of 10 is 5; so 5 marbles are half of a half, which is 1/4

simpler.hi: Gino, 20 tak pahunchne ke liye 5 kitni baar jodna padta hai. Utne hi barabar group bante hain.
simpler.en: Count how many times you add 5 to reach 20. That is how many equal groups there are.

viewCaption.hi: Jaal mein 20 kanche hain: do qatarein, har qatar mein 10. Har kanche ka apna khana hai, toh gin kar group banana aasaan hai.
viewCaption.en: The grid holds 20 marbles, two rows of ten. Each marble has its own box, so grouping them by counting is easy.

simpler.hi: Dono group ke kanche jodo: 10 aur 10, poore 20 kanche. Do barabar group saare kanche bana dete hain, isliye har group kanchon ka aadha hai.
simpler.en: Add the two groups' marbles: 10 and 10, all 20 marbles. Two equal groups make up all the marbles, so each group is half of them.

problemAlt.hi: Socho, 15 pencil 3 doston mein barabar baantni hain. Ek dost ko jitni milein, wahi 15 ka 1/3 hai.
problemAlt.en: Picture 15 pencils to be shared equally among 3 friends. What one friend gets is 1/3 of 15.

simpler.hi: Jaise 1/2 ka matlab 2 barabar group mein se ek, waise hi 1/3 ka matlab 3 barabar group mein se ek. Toh 15 pencil ke 3 barabar group socho, aur ek group dekho.
simpler.en: Just as 1/2 means one of 2 equal groups, 1/3 means one of 3 equal groups. So picture 15 pencils in 3 equal groups, and look at one group.

givens.hi: Kul ginti pata hai, fraction bhi pata hai; bas ek group ka size chahiye.
givens.en: We know the total and the fraction; we just need the size of one group.

find.en: how many pencils are in the 1/3 group

prompt.hi: 1/3 ke liye 15 pencil ko kitne barabar group mein baantoge?
prompt.en: For 1/3, into how many equal groups do you share the 15 pencils?

right.hi: Haan, 3 barabar group; unmein se ek group lena hai.
right.en: Yes, 3 equal groups; we take one of them.

do.hi: 1/3 ka neeche wala number group ginta hai
do.en: The bottom number of 1/3 counts the groups

steps.result: 3 barabar group, unmein se 1 group lena

why.hi: upar wala 1 batata hai kitne group lene hain
why.en: the top 1 says how many groups to take

simpler.hi: Socho 3 dost hain aur pencil sabko barabar milni hain. Ek dost ko jitni milein, wahi 1/3 hai.
simpler.en: Picture 3 friends who must get equal pencils. Whatever one friend gets is the 1/3.

prompt.hi: Tumhari baari: ek group mein kitni pencil aayengi?
prompt.en: Your turn: how many pencils go in one group?

reask.hi: 15 pencil 3 barabar group mein baanto, toh ek group mein kitni pencil aayengi?
reask.en: Share 15 pencils into 3 equal groups: how many pencils go in one group?

why.hi: 3 group mein 5-5 pencil rakhne se poori 15 ho jaati hain, 3 × 5 = 15
why.en: 5 pencils in each of 3 groups makes all 15, since 3 × 5 = 15

whyAlt.hi: 5, 10, 15: teen baar 5 jodne se 15 bante hain, toh har group mein 5
whyAlt.en: 5, 10, 15: adding 5 three times makes 15, so 5 in each group

simpler.hi: Pencil ek-ek karke 3 group mein rakho, baari-baari. Saari khatam, toh ek group gin lo.
simpler.en: Put the pencils one at a time into 3 groups, taking turns. When they are gone, count one group.

viewCaption.hi: Board par 15 pencil hain, har pencil ka apna khana. Inhe baari-baari ek-ek karke 3 group mein rakho, jab tak saari pencil khatam na ho jaayein.
viewCaption.en: The board has 15 pencils, each in its own box. Put them into 3 groups one at a time, taking turns, until all the pencils are used up.

why.hi: 3 group mein 5-5 pencil rakho toh poori 15 ho jaati hain, 3 × 5 = 15
why.en: 5 pencils in each of 3 groups makes all 15, 3 × 5 = 15

viewCaption.hi: Board par 15 pencil hain, har pencil ka apna khana. Abhi koi group nahi bana hai.
viewCaption.en: The board has 15 pencils, each in its own box. No group has been made yet.

prompt.hi: 18 laddoo 3 plate mein barabar rakhe gaye. Ravi ne 1 plate utha li. Ravi ke paas saare laddoo ka kaunsa fraction gaya?
prompt.en: 18 laddoos were put equally on 3 plates. Ravi picked up 1 plate. What fraction of all the laddoos went to Ravi?

reask.hi: 18 laddoo 3 barabar plate mein hain aur Ravi ek plate leta hai, toh Ravi ke paas saare laddoo ka kaunsa fraction hai?
reask.en: If 18 laddoos are on 3 equal plates and Ravi takes one plate, what fraction of all the laddoos does Ravi have?

did.hi: laddoo ki jagah plate gin kar Ravi ka fraction nikala
did.en: counted plates, not laddoos, to find Ravi's fraction

viewCaption.hi: Yeh 18 laddoo ek jaal mein hain: teen qatarein, har qatar mein chhe. Har qatar ko ek plate samjho.
viewCaption.en: These 18 laddoos are in a grid: three rows, six in each. Take each row as one plate.

why.hi: 18 laddoo 3 barabar plate mein the, har plate mein 6; Ravi ne 1 plate li, yaani 1/3
why.en: the 18 laddoos were on 3 equal plates, 6 on each; Ravi took 1 plate, so 1/3

whyShort.hi: Ravi ne 3 barabar plate mein se 1 li
whyShort.en: Ravi took 1 of 3 equal plates

whyAlt.hi: 3 barabar plate mein se Ravi ke paas ek plate hai; har plate mein kitne laddoo hain, isse fraction nahi badalta
whyAlt.en: Ravi has 1 of the 3 equal plates; how many laddoos sit on a plate does not change the fraction

simpler.hi: Socho, 1/3 wala tukda banane ke liye roti kitne tukdon mein katti. Phir dekho, Meena aur Sonu ne usse kam tukde kaate ya zyada.

reask.hi: 8 mein bati chocolate ka Farhan ka tukda, 2 mein bati utni hi badi chocolate ke Gita ke tukde se zyada hai ya kam?

viewCaption.hi: Dono chocolate ab do ek jitne bade circle hain: ek aath barabar tukdon mein, ek do mein.
viewCaption.en: The two chocolates are now two circles of the same size: one in eight equal pieces, one in two.

why.hi: 8 mein bati chocolate ka har tukda 1/8 hai, 2 mein bati ka 1/2; 1/8 chhota hai, toh Farhan ka tukda kam
why.en: shared by 8, each piece is 1/8; shared by 2, it is 1/2; 1/8 is smaller, so Farhan's piece is less

whyShort.hi: Farhan ka tukda 1/8, Gita ka 1/2; 1/8 chhota
whyShort.en: Farhan's piece is 1/8, Gita's 1/2; 1/8 is smaller

whyAlt.en: Gita's chocolate was shared by only 2 children, so she got half a chocolate; Farhan got one thin piece out of 8

answerViewCaption.hi: Line ke upar aath barabar gap hain aur pehla mark 1/8 par, line ke neeche do gap aur mark 1/2 par. 1/8 ka mark 0 ke bahut paas hai, isliye Farhan ka tukda kam hai.
answerViewCaption.en: Above the line are eight equal gaps with the first mark at 1/8, below it two gaps with the mark at 1/2. The 1/8 mark is very close to 0, so Farhan's piece is smaller.

simpler.hi: Board par dono patti dekho: pehli patti 8 tukdon mein, doosri patti 2 mein. Farhan ka ek tukda aur Gita ka ek tukda milao.
simpler.en: Look at both strips on the board: the first in 8 pieces, the second in 2. Compare one of Farhan's pieces with one of Gita's.

prompt.hi: Board par teen ek jaisi chocolate hain: pehli 4 barabar tukdon mein kati, doosri 10 mein, teesri 7 mein. Har chocolate ka ek tukda lo, 1/4, 1/10 aur 1/7, aur inhe sabse chhote se sabse bade tak lagao.

reask.hi: Teen ek jaisi chocolate ke 1/4, 1/10 aur 1/7 tukdon ko sabse chhote se sabse bade tak kaise lagaoge?

viewCaption.hi: Teeno chocolate ek jitni badi hain. Har chocolate ka pehla tukda dhyaan se dekho aur unki motai aapas mein milao.
viewCaption.en: The three chocolates are the same size. Look closely at the first piece of each chocolate and compare how thick they are.

why.hi: chocolate jitne zyada tukdon mein kate, tukda utna chhota; isliye pehle 1/10, phir 1/7, phir 1/4
why.en: the more pieces a chocolate is cut into, the smaller the piece, so 1/10 first, then 1/7, then 1/4

whyShort.hi: zyada tukde, chhota tukda: 1/10, phir 1/7, phir 1/4
whyShort.en: more pieces, smaller piece: 1/10, then 1/7, then 1/4

whyAlt.hi: socho 10 dost, 7 dost aur 4 dost ek-ek chocolate baant rahe hain; 10 dost waalon ka tukda sabse chhota, 4 dost waalon ka sabse bada
whyAlt.en: picture 10 friends, 7 friends and 4 friends each sharing a chocolate; the 10 friends get the smallest piece, the 4 friends the biggest

simpler.en: Look at each piece's bottom number: it tells how many equal pieces the chocolate was cut into. Then go from the thinnest piece to the thickest.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaise cake: ek ke 9 barabar tukde, ek ke 7 barabar tukde. Tumhe bada tukda chahiye, toh kis cake se loge?

viewCaption.hi: Dono cake ab ek jitni lambi patti hain: pehli nau barabar tukdon mein, doosri saat mein.
viewCaption.en: The two cakes are now strips of the same length: the first in nine equal pieces, the second in seven.

why.hi: 7 tukdon wala cake kam barabar tukdon mein kata, toh uska har tukda 9 wale ke tukde se bada hai
why.en: the 7-piece cake is cut into fewer equal pieces, so each of its pieces is bigger than the 9-piece cake's

whyShort.hi: kam tukde, bada tukda: 7 wale cake ka tukda bada
whyShort.en: fewer pieces, bigger piece: the 7-piece cake's is bigger

whyAlt.hi: 9 log ek cake baantein aur 7 log waisa hi cake, toh 7 waalon mein har ek ke haath mein bada tukda aata hai, kyunki log kam hain
whyAlt.en: if 9 people share one cake and 7 share one just like it, each of the 7 gets a bigger piece, because there are fewer people

answerViewCaption.hi: Dono pattiyan ek jitni lambi hain: pehli 9 barabar tukdon mein, doosri 7 mein. 7 wali patti ka har tukda lamba hai, isliye bada tukda 7 tukdon wale cake se milta hai.
answerViewCaption.en: Both strips are the same length: the first in 9 equal pieces, the second in 7. Each piece of the 7 strip is longer, so the bigger piece comes from the cake in 7 pieces.

simpler.hi: Dono cake ek jitne bade hain. Board par dekho, kis cake ke tukde mote dikhte hain.
simpler.en: Both cakes are the same size. Look at the board: which cake's pieces look thicker.

prompt.hi: Is circle ke 9 barabar tukde hain, aur 4 tukdon mein rang hai. Rangin tukde poore circle ka kaunsa fraction hain?

why.hi: circle ke saare 9 barabar tukde neeche wala number banate hain, aur rangin 4 upar wala number; bina rang ke 5 neeche wale number mein nahi jaate
why.en: all 9 equal pieces of the circle make the bottom number and the 4 coloured ones the top number; the 5 uncoloured ones never go in the bottom number

simpler.hi: Neeche wala number saare tukde ginta hai, rangin bhi aur bina rang ke bhi; upar wala sirf rangin.
simpler.en: The bottom number counts all the pieces, coloured and uncoloured; the top one only the coloured.
